name: Algolia
description: Protects against destructive Algolia operations like deleting indices, clearing objects, \ removing rules/synonyms, and deleting API keys.

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-indices-delete
destructive_patterns.description: algolia indices delete permanently removes an Algolia index.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an Algolia index permanently removes all searchable records, settings, \ rules, and synonyms. Search functionality for applications using this index will \ fail immediately. Re-indexing may require significant time and resources.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - algolia indices list: Review indices before deletion \ - Export index data using algolia indices browse \ - Create a replica or copy before deleting

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-indices-clear
destructive_patterns.description: algolia indices clear removes all objects from an Algolia index.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Clearing an Algolia index removes all searchable records while preserving settings, \ rules, and synonyms. Search will return no results until data is re-indexed. \ This is irreversible without re-indexing from source data.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export objects using algolia indices browse first \ - Use a staging index for testing \ - Delete specific objects instead of clearing all

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-rules-delete
destructive_patterns.description: algolia rules delete removes index rules.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Algolia rules removes search customizations like query rewrites, \ promotions, and filters. Search behavior may change unexpectedly for users \ relying on these rules for relevant results.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - algolia rules browse: Export rules before deletion \ - Disable rules temporarily instead of deleting \ - Test rule changes on a replica index first

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-synonyms-delete
destructive_patterns.description: algolia synonyms delete removes synonym entries.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting Algolia synonyms removes word associations that improve search matching. \ Users searching with alternative terms may no longer find expected results. \ Synonym configurations can take time to rebuild.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - algolia synonyms browse: Export synonyms before deletion \ - Test synonym changes on a replica index \ - Document synonym configurations for recovery

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-apikeys-delete
destructive_patterns.description: algolia apikeys delete removes API keys and can break integrations.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an Algolia API key immediately revokes access for all applications using \ it. Search and indexing operations will fail with authentication errors. The key \ cannot be recovered after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - algolia apikeys list: Review keys and their usage \ - Create new API keys before deleting old ones \ - Rotate keys by updating applications first

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-sdk-delete-index
destructive_patterns.description: Algolia SDK deleteIndex removes an index.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The deleteIndex SDK method permanently removes an Algolia index and all its \ contents. This includes all records, settings, rules, and synonyms. Production \ search functionality will fail immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Use browseObjects to export data first \ - Copy to a backup index before deleting \ - Add confirmation prompts in application code

destructive_patterns.name: algolia-sdk-clear-objects
destructive_patterns.description: Algolia SDK clearObjects removes all records from an index.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The clearObjects SDK method removes all searchable records from an index while \ keeping configuration intact. Search results will be empty until re-indexing \ completes. This cannot be undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Export objects using browseObjects first \ - Use deleteObjects for targeted removal \ - Test on a replica index before production
